summary: Iteration 19 tested the product count, the {kota} free-shipping text and the COD auto-cancel chip. Backend, new suite tests/test_pgs_iter19_count_kota_cod_expiry.py: 6 of 7 pass. GET /api/products/count returns {count:6618}. That matches a Mongo count of products outside inactive stores, ignores X-Store-Id, and is not shadowed by /products/{id} (the detail route still works). GET /home-settings has subtitle 'Area {kota} & sekitarnya...'. Legacy text 'Area Sidoarjo ...' is rewritten to 'Area {kota} ...' on read, and custom text is kept; the original settings doc was restored. The one failure: expires_at (and the other datetimes) is serialized without a timezone, e.g. '2026-11-10T10:23:58.818000'. Frontend at 375x667, home as guest: home-search-placeholder shows 'Cari dari 6.618 produk…'. free-shipping-subtitle shows 'Area Sidoarjo ...' for PGS Sidoarjo, 'Area Jombang ...' after store-switch -> pick-store-pgs-jombang, and 'Area Jember ...' for Jember, and goes back to Sidoarjo. Admin (admin@pgs.id): the home-settings {kota} hint is visible, the preview reads 'Area cabang pilihan & sekitarnya...', and the admin products placeholder reads 'Cari produk dari 6.618 produk'. Seller orders (sidoarjo@pgs.id) with a browser in UTC: the urgent order (expires_at set to now+3h in Mongo) has a red border (rgb 239,68,68), a red chip and the text 'Hampir batal otomatis · sisa ±3 jam'. The normal order has a grey chip 'Batal otomatis 10 Nov 2026, 10.24' and the default border. BUG: with the browser timezone set to Asia/Jakarta (the real users' zone), the same urgent order shows 'sisa ±1 jam'. Its real time left is 3h; the code computes -4h and clamps it to 1. codHoursLeft uses new Date(expires_at) on a string with no timezone, so it is read as local time, while fmtDate appends 'Z'. In WIB every hours-left value is 7h too small, so orders with up to about 13h left are wrongly marked urgent. Regression: iter18 and iter15 suites pass 23/23 when run one at a time (-n0); under xdist 3 tests fail because the parallel tests share stock and server restarts, which is not a product bug. No console or page errors. No deprecated Expo packages in the files reviewed. Test orders were cancelled.

minor.issue: expires_at and created_at are returned as naive ISO strings without 'Z' or an offset (Mongo returns naive UTC datetimes). The frontend has to guess the timezone, which caused the frontend bug below.

ui_bugs.issue: new Date(o.expires_at) reads the naive UTC string as device-local time. In Asia/Jakarta (UTC+7) the hours left are 7h too small: an order with 3h left shows 'sisa ±1 jam', and orders with 6–13h left are wrongly marked urgent with a red border. Verified in Playwright with timezone_id=Asia/Jakarta. Reference: /app/frontend/app/seller/orders.tsx:22

issues: The urgent chip has white 12px text on #EF4444, a contrast ratio of about 3.8:1, below WCAG AA 4.5:1. A darker red (e.g. #DC2626 or #B91C1C) would pass.
Overdue orders (expires_at already passed but the auto-cancel task has not run yet) still show 'sisa ±1 jam' because of Math.max(1, ...). 'Segera dibatalkan' would be clearer.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the timezone handling of COD hours-left. In seller/orders.tsx codHoursLeft, parse with the same normalisation as fmtDate: add 'Z' when the string has no offset. Better: add a shared parseDate() in src/utils/date.ts. Also consider having the backend serialize datetimes as tz-aware UTC (e.g. tz_aware=True on the Motor client, or a field serializer that adds +00:00).
Minor: use a darker red for the urgent chip background to meet contrast requirements, and handle negative hours left ('Segera dibatalkan').
Minor: on the home screen productCount is fetched once in useEffect([]) and is not refreshed on pull-to-refresh.

Design note: promo.get_home rewrites any saved 'Area Sidoarjo' to 'Area {kota}' on read, so an admin can no longer deliberately save text naming only Sidoarjo. Consider a one-time migration instead of rewriting on every read.
critical_code_review_comments: seller/orders.tsx:22 uses new Date(iso) directly while src/utils/date.ts fmtDate normalises it. Two ways of parsing the same field is the root cause of the bug.
/products/count is declared before /products/{product_id} in server.py:686, so the routes are ordered correctly.
home-sections FreeShippingBanner replaces {kota} case-insensitively and falls back to 'cabang pilihan'. Correct.

success_rate.backend: 86% (6/7; the failure is the naive datetime serialization)
success_rate.frontend: 90% (all requested flows pass in UTC; the urgency calculation is wrong in non-UTC timezones)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with -n0 for the order and stock suites (iter15, iter18); xdist parallelism causes false failures. To check the timezone fix in Playwright, use browser.new_context(timezone_id='Asia/Jakarta'), then run ui_iter19_helper.py setup and cleanup.
rca_of_issue: The backend stores expires_at as a UTC datetime and Mongo returns it naive, so the response has no timezone ('2026-11-10T10:23:58'). ECMAScript reads date-time strings without an offset as local time. On a WIB device the expiry therefore lands 7h earlier and hours left = real - 7. Repro: create a pickup COD order, set expires_at to now+3h, then open /seller/orders in a Jakarta-timezone browser: the chip reads 'sisa ±1 jam'. Mitigation: normalise with 'Z' when there is no offset, or serialize tz-aware datetimes from the backend.
